newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Dec 9.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Dec 9.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Parramatta president Alan Overton - whose future on the board is dependent on the response of football club members to his support for the Australian Rugby League - has described tomorrow night's football club annual general meeting as ultimately a vote on whether the Eels remain with the ARL or join Super League next season. Page 27.

Police are investigating a series of attacks on the Sydney home of SBS-TV commentator and former Australian soccer player John Warren. Warren believes the attacks are linked to his support for soccer clubs being able to keep their soccer league emblems in the face of stiff opposition from Soccer Australia, and his criticism of the appointment of former English manager Terry Venables as Socceroo coach. Page 27.

Inspired by a successful performance at the Atlanta Olympics, where they equalled their best result of fourth, the Australian Boomers basketball coach Barry Barnes has designed a four-year plan to turn the team's medal dreams into a reality. Page 26.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Soccer's world governing body, FIFA, indicated on Saturday that despite being unhappy with its treatment at the Atlanta Olympic Games, where all of the soccer games were played away from Atlanta, it would not act upon an earlier threat to
withdraw from th Olympics, and would participate in the Sydney Games. Page 28.

David Campese's illustrious career finally ended at Twickenham on Saturday, with a 70,000-plus crowd there for the final game of the Australian tour to witness Campese's last game with the Wallabies - a game which saw Australia win 39-12 against the Barbaians, with Campo scoring the Wallabies' third of four tries. Page 29.

Coming into yesterday's fourth round of the Uncle Tobys Super Series in Adelaide amid accusations of being past it, iron men Trevor Hendy and Guy Andrews proved their detractors wrong by coming first and second respectively in the Man-on Man event. Page 3.
THE AGE

Australian golfers Terry Price, Stuart Appleby and Brad Hughes were tied at 50th place on one-over-par 289 with two rounds to play in the fourth round of the US PGA Tour qualifying tournament yesterday, however, fellow Australians Anthony
Painter and Mark Hensby did not survive the cut. Page 7.

Melbourne Reds director Andy Karetsky said yesterday the club was most disappointed with the Australian Baseball League appeals board decision to allow former Reds hitter Greg Jelks to play for Perth, and has not ruled out court action over the ruling. Page 12.

Scotland's Peter Nicol fought back from the brink of defeat yesterday to down Australia's world number two Rodney Eyles 13-15, 15-10, 7-15, 17-15, 15-13 in a dramatic final of the A$132,000 Mahindra Squash International in Bombay - the richest tournament in the squash circuit outside the World Open. Page 12.
THE HERALD SUN

Thanks to a career-best 5-33 off 9.3 overs from Shane Warne and Mark Waugh delivering an unbeaten 83, Australia last night achieved a convincing eight wicket win against the West Indies in their one-day game at the Sydney Cricket Ground. Page 80.

Australians dominated yesterday's sessions of a junior five-nation weight-lifting competition at De La Salle College in Malvern, with Chris Rae, 16, from Adelaide and Anthony Martin, 17, from Ipswich demonstrating their skills and capability for the 1998 Commonwealth Games with strong performances. Page 74.

After plans to reschedule two rained-out games against Hunter Eagles were dumped, Melbourne Monarchs baseball manager Jon Deeble yesterday called for the Australian Baseball League to implement a make-up day for interrupted games in next year's schedule. age 72.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

According to Australian Jockey Club betting manager Craig Nugent, the New South Wales racing industry is advancing with negotiations to increase racing's coverage on free-to-air television - and from next February the State's punters will
finally be able to watch thoroughbred, harness and greyhound racing seven days a week on an exclusive pay-TV channel. Page 31.

Victoria Racing club stewards have swabbed Fabulous Friscoe and Judge Dredd - two horses trained at Caulfield by Jim Conlan - after both were sent out favourites in their respective races at Flemington yesterday and failed dismally. Conlan claims he heard from a member of his staff that there may have been unauthorised persons in his stable area on Saturday night. Page 31.

Following an alleged brawl with police in Melbourne shortly after midnight on Saturday night, Collingwood president Kevin Rose last night said the Australian Football League club could delist the three players involved after it holds an inquiry into the incident. Page 31.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
